• Large legacy codebases refactored under a live user base.

• Desktop distribution: installers, auto-update, signing and notarisation, licence enforcement, crash reporting.

• Plugin hosts (VST3/AU/LV2) desirable.

• Led a horizontal or guild where engineers report elsewhere day-to-day.

• Hands-on with agentic coding stacks applied to C++.

• Open-source experience desirable.

• Muse leadership match.

About Fello :
Fello is a profitable, hyper-growth, VC-backed B2B SaaS company building the agentic real estate platform of the future.
Our platform combines data intelligence, marketing automation, and conversational AI to help real estate teams engage smarter and scale faster. If you're excited about building an AI product that's changing how an entire industry works, you'll fit right in.
About You:
You want to work on a system of agents that work together. Some of them talk to customers, and many of them never say a word to anyone. They interpret, decide, and pass work to each other, and you understand that the quality of the whole system depends on every link in that chain holding up in production. Making that behave reliably, at scale, with real customers on the other end, is the problem you want to own.
You treat prompts as engineering artifacts, not text you tweak until a demo works. If you've ever shipped a prompt change that fixed one case and quietly broke nine others, you know why the evaluation layer matters as much as the prompt itself. And if you get a small thrill from a regression suite going green after a nasty bug, you'll feel at home here.
You'll also recognize how we work. We measure what we ship: changes come with evidence behind them, a dataset, a score, a clear before and after. We ship weekly, so ideas get tested against real production behavior quickly rather than studied at length. Craft matters, and so does rigor - getting an agent to sound right is satisfying, but proving it still sounds right across thousands of conversations is the actual work.
The surface area grows every quarter with new agents, new channels, and new products. You'll own a meaningful slice of it from day one.
You Will:

•
Design prompts for agents that work together. Define what each agent knows, what it's allowed to decide, what it hands off, and what it must never do, including the contracts between agents that keep the system coherent end to end.

•
Build the evaluation layer. Every prompt you ship comes with a dataset and a regression suite. You'll curate test cases from real production behavior, write evaluator prompts, define scoring rubrics that actually track business outcomes, and catch regressions before customers do.

•
Make the system observable. Tracing, prompt versioning, datasets, experiments, scoring. You'll instrument what isn't yet instrumented and use the data to find where agents are actually struggling, which is often somewhere other than where we'd guess.

•
Debug production behavior. When something goes wrong in a live interaction, you'll pull the trace, isolate the root cause, ship the fix, and add the case to the eval set so it never returns.

•
Work across different models. We use more than one model, because different jobs call for different tradeoffs in reasoning, speed, and cost. Each one follows instructions a little differently, so a prompt that works well on one may need real rework on another. You'll help choose which model fits which job, and keep agent behavior stable when we switch.

•
Work with dynamic context. Our prompts are assembled at runtime from live data. You'll design the logic that decides what an agent sees and when, and you'll find that many "prompt problems" turn out to be context problems.

•
Partner across the company. Product, engineering, sales, and support. You'll turn a vague "this interaction felt off" into a reproducible test case, a fix, and a metric that proves it's fixed.

Position Location: Remote - work virtually from anywhere in the United States

The Engineering Manager - Design provides leadership, expertise, and delegates work for design document deliverables for building automation system (BAS), electrical power monitoring system (EPMS), and software integration design projects in hyperscale data center and similar mission critical / technology sectors. This role leads a team of BAS / EPMS engineers, ensuring consistent delivery and quality across multiple MEP design programs by integrating lessons learned and leading the QAQC effort.

This position will work with internal and external MEP/FP trade engineers, equipment representatives, product vendors, and BIM / Revit / AutoCAD production resources.

The Engineering Manager - Design will be self-directed on day-to-day work and receive high level instruction on new projects, tasks or assignments. This person will communicate and operate in line with organizational goals / values, and departmental objectives.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Develop and Execute Building Automation Systems Engineering Solutions (25%)

• Serve as client program lead, project trade lead, and SME for the BAS and EPMS scope for one or more projects and / or programs.

• Develop client standards, basis of design (BOD), perform feasibility studies, and assist clients with building automation roadmaps

• Lead designs for DDC and PLC based BAS and EPMS systems

• Design controls network / system architecture including IT / OT requirements

• Select instrumentation, sensors, actuators, valves and other field devices

• Coordinate with equipment, system, and product vendors for building automation interface requirements

• Create and review project book and sheet specifications

• Create and review sequence of operations

• Create and review system diagrams and point / alarm lists

• Work closely with client IT departments for network design, interface details, and security requirements

• Provide direction on engineering production aspects with internal and external Revit / BIM resources

Training / Technical Firm Standards Development / Improvement of Policies and Procedures (30%)

• Develop, maintain, and enforce organizational design standards, templates, and best practices for BAS / EPMS design projects alongside leadership

• Mentor and train staff on technical competencies, software tools, and project workflows

• Promote continuous improvement through lessons learned sessions on completed projects

• Perform QAQC reviews for all project milestones on projects / programs where they are not lead engineer

Construction Related Process, Deliverables and Submissions (15%)

• Accountable for design document deliverables for design phases including Schematic Design (SD), Design Development (DD), Issue For Permit (IFP), Issue For Construction (IFC)

• Lead planning and execution of Construction Administration (CA) phase activities remote and on site

• Lead building automation focused design reviews and page turns
